# Known gaps

<!-- Generated by internal/providers/contractcoverage; do not edit. Regenerate with: go test ./internal/providers/contractcoverage/ -update -->

Every response field, event, finish reason, error mapping or billing input a provider adapter loses, as
the contract tests allowlist it: each `known gap <ID>: <reason>` in the fixtures' `meta.json` and `case.json`,
the speech sessions, the `spec_allowlist*.json` files of the official-spec checks, and the provider tests' gap
tables. A gap is allowlisted, not fixed: the suites fail when it changes or goes away, and a fix deletes its
entries. One line per ID: the loss (the reason's first sentence, or the reviewed summary in
`internal/providers/contractcoverage/gap_summaries.json` where definitions word it differently) and where it
is defined (provider, then model, model/case, `spec <subset>` or test file, with a count when more than one).
Coverage by provider and endpoint is in [CONTRACT_COVERAGE.md](CONTRACT_COVERAGE.md).

| T4 | The stream parser drops thinking entirely (thinking blocks, thinking_delta, signature_delta): streamed responses carry no reasoning_content and no signatures, unlike the non-stream path | anthropic: claude-opus-5-5 ×3, claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929 ×3, spec anthropic/stream ×3 |

| S1 | stop_reason "refusal" has no mapping and falls back to "stop", so a declined or cut-off response looks like a normal completion; "content_filter" is the canonical reason | anthropic: claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929, spec anthropic/messages, spec anthropic/stream |
| S2 | The refusal category and explanation (stop_details) are dropped, and stop_reason refusal itself is unmapped, so a caller cannot tell a refusal from a normal stop | anthropic: claude-opus-5-5 ×2, spec anthropic/messages, spec anthropic/stream |

| X9 | the native passthrough does not forward the upstream's response headers (CreateAnthropicMessage and StreamAnthropicMessage return only a body and a status), so a client such as Claude Code, whose SDK honours retry-after, never sees it, nor anthropic-ratelimit-* or request-id | server: contract_anthropic_native_test.go |

| X12 | diagnostics (cache_miss_reason: why the prompt cache missed) is dropped | anthropic: spec anthropic/messages, spec anthropic/stream |

| G28 | a failed generation (UNEXPECTED_TOOL_CALL, TOO_MANY_TOOL_CALLS, MISSING_THOUGHT_SIGNATURE, MALFORMED_RESPONSE, NO_IMAGE, IMAGE_OTHER) falls back to "stop": the caller sees a normal, often empty, completion with no sign the model failed | gemini: spec gemini/generate_content ×6, spec vertex/generate_content ×4 |
| G29 | logprobs are neither requested (logprobs / top_logprobs are not sent as responseLogprobs / logprobs) nor translated (logprobsResult, avgLogprobs), although the canonical choice has a logprobs field | gemini: spec gemini/generate_content ×2, spec vertex/generate_content ×2 |
| G30 | citation metadata (recitation sources with spans, URIs and licenses; citationSources on the Gemini API, citations on Vertex AI) is dropped; code recitations carry license information a client may be required to show | gemini: spec gemini/generate_content, spec vertex/generate_content |
| G31 | audioTranscription (the text of generated audio) is dropped; the canonical audio content part has no transcript, though OpenAI's message audio carries one | gemini: spec gemini/generate_content, spec vertex/generate_content |
| G32 | the upstream functionCall.id is dropped; the gateway numbers calls call_N itself and never sends functionResponse.id back, so parallel calls to the same function are matched by order alone | gemini: spec gemini/generate_content, spec vertex/generate_content |
| G33 | modelStatus (model stage and retirement time) is dropped, so a client is never told its model is deprecated or about to be retired | gemini: spec gemini/generate_content |
| GR2 | request side: a client's thinking_budget always becomes thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget, whatever the model, so on a model that takes thinkingLevel only (Gemini 4 Argon) every request with a thinking budget fails with this 400 | gemini: gemini-4-argon/error_thinking_budget |

| ID | loss | defined in |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | parseStreamPayload decodes the InvokeModelWithResponseStream chunk envelope {"bytes": <base64 Anthropic event>} as if it were the event and never reads bytes, so every InvokeModel stream yields no content, no finish_reason and no usage | bedrock: anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 ×2, spec bedrock/invoke_stream |
| B2 | Converse reasoningContent (reasoning text, signature, redactedContent) is dropped, stream and non-stream, so no reasoning_content or thinking_blocks reach the client and a Claude tool-use turn with reasoning cannot be replayed | bedrock: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 ×4, spec bedrock/converse, spec bedrock/converse_stream, us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 ×4 |
| B3 | thinking and redacted_thinking blocks are dropped whole on the InvokeModel path, signatures included; Anthropic requires them passed back unchanged in a tool-use turn | bedrock: anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 ×3, spec anthropic/messages ×2, spec anthropic/stream ×4 |
| B4 | stopReason guardrail_intervened falls back to "stop", so a response a guardrail blocked looks like a normal completion; "content_filter" is the canonical reason | bedrock: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6, spec bedrock/converse, spec bedrock/converse_stream |
| B5 | stopReason content_filtered falls back to "stop", so a response the model's content filters blocked looks like a normal completion; "content_filter" is the canonical reason | bedrock: spec bedrock/converse, spec bedrock/converse_stream, us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 |
| B6 | stopReason model_context_window_exceeded falls back to "stop" on both APIs; the response was truncated, so "length" is the honest canonical reason | bedrock: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6, spec anthropic/messages, spec anthropic/stream, spec bedrock/converse, spec bedrock/converse_stream |
| B7 | this stop reason has no mapping and falls back to "stop" (lookupStopReason), so a malformed generation, a paused server-tool turn or a refusal looks like a normal completion | bedrock: spec anthropic/messages ×2, spec anthropic/stream ×2, spec bedrock/converse ×2, spec bedrock/converse_stream ×2 |
| B8 | Converse prompt-cache read and write tokens (cacheReadInputTokens, cacheWriteInputTokens) are dropped instead of counted in prompt_tokens / cached_tokens, so usage and cost under-count cached requests (0 today: the gateway never sends a cachePoint) | bedrock: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 ×4, spec bedrock/converse ×2, spec bedrock/converse_stream ×2 |
| B9 | InvokeModel prompt-cache read and write tokens are dropped instead of counted in prompt_tokens / cached_tokens, stream and non-stream, so usage and cost under-count cached requests | bedrock: anthropic.claude-opus-5-5 ×4, spec anthropic/messages ×2, spec anthropic/stream ×4 |
| B10 | request side: the Converse request (converseRequest) has no additionalModelRequestFields or additionalModelResponseFieldPaths, so a model-specific parameter (Claude's thinking budget, Nova's reasoning config) cannot reach a Converse model, and the model-specific response fields it would return never come back | bedrock: contract_surface_test.go |
| B13 | every model ID that is not an inference profile goes to InvokeModel with an Anthropic Messages body, so a base model ID of another vendor (amazon.nova-*, meta.llama*) gets a body it rejects | bedrock: contract_surface_test.go |
| B14 | isInferenceProfile knows the us., eu., ap. and global. prefixes only, so apac., jp., au. and us-gov. profiles go to InvokeModel with an Anthropic Messages body (a Claude profile's stream is then empty, gap B1; any other vendor's profile rejects the body, gap B13), and ap. matches no AWS geography | bedrock: contract_surface_test.go |
| B15 | parseBedrockError types an error by its HTTP status alone and never reads x-amzn-ErrorType, so this exception gets the wrong canonical type (AccessDenied: authentication_error, not permission_error; ModelTimeout and ModelError: invalid_request_error, not a timeout or an upstream failure; ModelNotReady: rate_limit_error, indistinguishable from throttling); see the error_* contract cases | bedrock: spec bedrock/converse_errors ×4 |
| B16 | A mid-stream exception's payload is not decoded: every exception becomes a 502 upstream_error with the raw JSON as its message, so a throttlingException (429), modelTimeoutException (408) or modelStreamErrorException (424) is retried, failed over and counted as a server error | bedrock: anthropic.claude-opus-5-5/stream_exception_model_timeout, anthropic.claude-opus-5-5/stream_exception_throttling, global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6/stream_exception_model_stream_error, global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6/stream_exception_throttling, spec bedrock/converse_stream ×5, spec bedrock/invoke_stream ×6 |
| B17 | A ModelErrorException's originalStatusCode and resourceName are dropped; parseBedrockError keeps only the message, so the canonical error cannot say whether the model failed with a 4xx or a 5xx | bedrock: global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 ×2 |
| B18 | a bare ARN (application-inference-profile, inference-profile or foundation-model) is cut at its first "/" as if its head were a gateway provider name, so only the resource ID goes upstream, to InvokeModel, which knows no such model | bedrock: contract_surface_test.go |
| B19 | citations are dropped on both APIs (Converse citationsContent blocks and citation deltas; InvokeModel content[].citations, which bedrockContentBlock has no field for), so grounded answers reach the client with no sources | bedrock: spec anthropic/messages, spec anthropic/stream, spec bedrock/converse, spec bedrock/converse_stream |
| B20 | Server-side tools are not translated on either API (Converse server_tool_use toolUse and toolResult blocks, starts and deltas; InvokeModel server_tool_use and *_tool_result blocks and the code-execution container): their calls and results are dropped | bedrock: spec anthropic/messages ×12, spec anthropic/stream ×12, spec bedrock/converse ×7, spec bedrock/converse_stream ×3 |
| B21 | InvokeModel stop_details (the refusal category and explanation) is dropped, so there is no way to tell why a response was refused | bedrock: spec anthropic/messages, spec anthropic/stream |
| B22 | billing details beyond input and output tokens are dropped: the per-TTL cache-write breakdown, thinking tokens, server-tool request counts, the service tier, speed and inference geography (InvokeModel usage), and Converse's serviceTier, performanceConfig and usage.cacheDetails, so priority, flex, latency-optimized, fast-mode and 1h-cache pricing cannot be seen | bedrock: spec anthropic/messages ×6, spec anthropic/stream ×8, spec bedrock/converse ×3, spec bedrock/converse_stream ×3 |
| B23 | InvokeModel diagnostics (cache_miss_reason: why the prompt cache missed) is dropped | bedrock: spec anthropic/messages, spec anthropic/stream |
| B25 | image output (a Converse image content block, a ConverseStream image start or delta) is dropped; converseContentPart decodes image only because it is also the request type, and translateConverseResponse / parseConverseEvent keep text and toolUse alone | bedrock: spec bedrock/converse ×3, spec bedrock/converse_stream ×2 |
| B26 | content-block members other than text, toolUse, reasoningContent (B2), citationsContent (B19), toolResult (B20) and image (B25) are dropped by translateConverseResponse (and reported); the ContentBlock union serves requests and responses alike, and whether a model returns these is unverified | bedrock: spec bedrock/converse ×8 |

## Cohere

| ID | loss | defined in |
|---|---|---|
| K1 | The stream parser reads finish_reason and usage from the top level of message-end, where Cohere never sends them (they are under delta), so every stream ends with "stop" whatever the real reason and reports no usage | cohere: command-a-03-2025 ×3, command-a-reasoning-08-2025 ×3, contract_test.go, spec cohere/chat_stream ×7 |
| K2 | cached prompt tokens are dropped instead of reported as prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, so cache hits are invisible to cost accounting | cohere: command-a-03-2025, command-a-reasoning-08-2025, spec cohere/chat |
| K3 | Citations (cited span, text and the tool output or document it came from) are dropped, stream and non-stream; the canonical message has annotations but the adapter emits none | cohere: command-a-03-2025 ×2, spec cohere/chat, spec cohere/chat_stream |
| K4 | A reasoning model's thinking is dropped (thinking content blocks and deltas) instead of becoming reasoning_content | cohere: command-a-reasoning-08-2025 ×4, spec cohere/chat, spec cohere/chat_stream |
| K5 | The tool plan (the model's stated reasoning before its tool calls) is dropped, stream and non-stream; Cohere expects it back as tool_plan on the next turn | cohere: command-a-03-2025 ×2, spec cohere/chat, spec cohere/chat_stream |
| K6 | finish_reason TIMEOUT falls back to "stop", so a generation the API cut off for time looks complete; "length" is the nearest canonical reason | cohere: command-a-03-2025, spec cohere/chat |
| K7 | A failed generation reaches the client as a success: lookupCohereFinishReason maps ERROR to "stop", and a stream that fails mid-generation loses its error message | cohere: command-a-03-2025, command-a-03-2025/finish_error, command-a-03-2025/stream_error |
| K8 | translateRerankResponse reports billed_units.input_tokens as search_units, and cohereBilledUnits has no search_units field, so a search-unit bill is read as 0 (priced at the one-unit fallback) and a token-billed rerank is priced as that many searches | cohere: rerank-v5.0-pro, rerank-v5.0-pro/rerank_basic, rerank-v5.0-pro/rerank_relevant_spans, spec cohere/rerank |
| K9 | encoding_format and dimensions are not forwarded: the adapter always asks for embedding_types ["float"] and never sends output_dimension, so a client asking for base64 or a smaller vector gets default-size float arrays | cohere: embed-v5.0-fast/embed_base64, spec cohere/embed ×5 |
| K10 | ListModels returns nil without calling GET /v1/models, so the gateway cannot list or validate the models a key can use | cohere: command-a-03-2025/list_models |
| K11 | the error id is dropped (parseCohereError reads only message), so a failed request cannot be traced with Cohere support | cohere: command-a-03-2025, embed-v5.0-fast, rerank-v5.0-pro, spec cohere/errors |
| K12 | logprobs are dropped: translateRequest does not forward the canonical request's logprobs, and the adapter's types have no field for the response's, so a client asking for token log probabilities gets none | cohere: spec cohere/chat, spec cohere/chat_stream |
| K13 | latent: the spec types every billed and token count as number, and the adapter decodes them into int; every documented example and fixture carries whole numbers, but a fractional count (the Python SDK models them as floats) would fail json.Unmarshal of the whole response and turn a 200 into a 502 | cohere: spec cohere/chat ×4, spec cohere/embed ×2, spec cohere/rerank ×2 |
